clues: This is considered by paleopathologists to be the oldest known rheumatic disorder. Evidence of this has been discovered in dinosaur fossils and early prehistoric mammals

This spinal disorder has been found in several ancient Egyptian mummies, including Pharaoh Merneptah, his father Ramesses II, and Amenhotep III, although it is not strictly hereditary. These mummies were misdiagnosed for years until they went through modern CT scans.

This is a non-inflammatory condition where ligaments and tendons harden and turn into bone. On X-rays, the flowing bone spurs along the side of the spine can look like wax dripping down the side of a candle.

When analyzing the skeletal remains of the Lake Woodland indigenous peoples of North America, who lived roughly between 500 and 1000AD, paleopathologists noticed a stark uptick in destructive bone lesions compared to earlier eras. Researchers hypothesize that as these ancient societies shifted toward intensive agriculture, they inadvertently dug up and inhaled massive amounts of spores from this organism, contributing to shortened lifespans observed during the agricultural transition

Dogs, especially hunting, sporting, and large breeds that spend time sniffing and digging in wet soil, are up to ten times more susceptible to this fungus than humans. It is not typically contagious from animals to humans

In the chilly environment of outdoor dirt and wood, this grows as a harmless, fuzzy mold. However, once its tiny spores are inhaled into the warm human or animal body, they morph into large, multiplying yeasts that can invade tissue. Under the microscope, the yeast can be easily recognized by its unique 'broad-based buds'.

A natural form of this medication from was the powdered seeds of Mucuna pruriens (velvet bean) used in ancient India around 300BCE. It wasn't until 1911 that it was synthesized in a lab and a Swiss biochemist isolated the pure L-isomer from fava beans. Curious about its effects, he ingested 2.5 grams of it himself and vomited violently. As a result, no one bothered to patent it.

This drug was immortalized in Oliver Sacks's 1973 book and subsequent 1990 movie, Awakenings, starring Robin Williams and Robert De Niro. In 1969, Sacks administered the experimental drug to patients at a New York hospital who had been frozen in a catatonic, statue-like state for decades. While the drug initially awakened them to a normal life, the patients developed severe involuntary movements, hallucinations, and chaotic mood swings

By the mid-1970s, scientists paired this drug with carbidopa, which blocks conversion into dopamine in the bloodstream, allowing it to safely cross the blood-brain barrier. This eliminated the severe associated vomiting giving the combination medication its name meaning 'without emesis'.

In the 4th century BC, Hippocrates wrote about the two primary pathways that this disease develops although it may have also been described in the Chester Beatty VI medical papyrus from Egypt around 1200BC.

In 1916, German bacteriologist Hans Conrad Julius Reiter described this condition which led to it being widely named Reiter's syndrome. Decades later, it was revealed that Reiter was an early member of the Nazi party and oversaw fatal human experiments on concentration camp prisoners. This led to his name being stripped from the disease.

Modern retrospective medical analyses suggest Columbus suffered from this disease. At the age of 41, he began having episodes of joint pain, fevers, and an aggressive eye inflammation so severe that his eyes frequently bled. Experts believe he may have had HLA-B27 and contracted food poisoning, likely from Shigella or Salmonella, that triggered a severe, lifelong systematic autoimmune response

This is technically a prodrug that enters cells harmlessly. Once inside, flavoproteins attack the drug, converting it into highly reactive molecules that shred the cell's DNA, RNA, cell wall proteins, and metabolic enzymes

The original form of this consisted of microcrystals and was absorbed very quickly, causing severe GI upset and required dosing four times a day. To fix this, scientists created a macrocrystalline formulation which slowed down absorption and decreased stomach upset. They also combined it with a slow-release matrix so the medication only had to be taken twice a day. This gave birth to the brand name of the antibiotic

When swallowed, the body processes this drug so rapidly that it clears from the bloodstream almost immediately, failing to reach antibacterial levels in blood or tissue. However, because the kidneys filter it, the drug builds up in massive, concentrated doses inside the bladder.
